title: I retired early at 31 and left the US for Ecuador. Life is cheaper, and I get more time with my baby.
summary:
This as-told-to essay is based on a conversation with Johnston Osagie, 32, who retired early and moved from Tennessee to Ecuador with his wife and daughter.
Suddenly, another 10 years of trading the best hours of my life for work instead of family didn't sound so appealing.
I quit my job at Amazon in January, and my wife and I moved from Nashville to Cuenca, Ecuador, in February.
Because I wanted to retire early, I was aggressive with my portfolio allocations to achieve faster growth.
I handed in my notice in January, a month before we moved to Ecuador.

title: US lawmakers ask Trump administration to stop deportation of Afghans
summary:
The Trump administration has forcibly sent at least 25,000 people to third countries, according to a tally by nonprofits Refugees International and Human Rights First.
Since taking office, Trump has attempted to put an end to resettlement programmes for Afghans started by former President Joe Biden.
The Trump administration has instituted record-low quotas for asylum applications globally.
Trump ordered a halt to processing applications from Afghans after a man from Afghanistan allegedly shot two National Guardsmen in Washington, DC, in November 2025.
The Trump administration also included Afghan nationals in a blanket visa ban earlier this year, saying it would review immigration applications filed by anyone from the country.

title: Why Immigration Agents Don’t Quit in Protest
summary:
Much of the outcry stirred by the harsh policies of the first Trump Administration was quelled by Joe Biden’s promise of a more measured approach.
Still, there was a feeling among immigration agents that they were being shackled by the new Administration.
By 2024, the Border Patrol had lost a quarter of its workforce, with many longtime agents opting for early retirement.
The operation was so unpopular with the rank and file that Border Patrol and ICE struggled to find personnel for the deployment.
“We can’t always support what happens just because it’s one of us,” a Border Patrol agent had told a private group chat in the wake of Pretti’s killing.

title: Indicted ICE officer accused of intentionally striking man expected to surrender on Monday
summary:
The Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer accused of intentionally striking a man in Houston earlier this month is expected to surrender on Monday morning, his attorney, David Lindenmuth told ABC News.
Mario Alberto Morales was indicted by a grand jury in Houston on a charge of second-degree aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, according to the Harris County District Attorney's Office.
Authorities say that’s when the vehicle struck Parra Hernandez and then came to a stop.
According to Lindenmuth, Morales is a former corrections officer who enlisted in the Army.
Morales also worked as a detention and processing officer at the Port Isabel Detention Center and worked with DHS as an ICE contractor, Lindenmuth said.

title: At least seven migrants die on boat bound for Canary Islands amid storm
summary:

Rescuers reached the boat early on Monday, about 150km from Arrecife.
Five bodies are missing overboard and two have been recovered.

title: UK to double wait for permanent residency, with exemptions for care workers
summary:
Share UK to double wait for permanent residency, with exemptions for care workers on social mediaThe United Kingdom has revised its immigration rules, doubling the time most foreign workers must wait to qualify for permanent residency to 10 years and making refugees who arrive on “small boats” wait as long as 30 years.
Permanent residency, known in the UK as indefinite leave to remain, carries the right to work, study, use the free National Health Service and claim welfare benefits.
The new rules, set to take effect next year, tie eligibility for permanent residency to income.
“Those who don’t play by the rules will be refused or wait longer.”Care workers, refugeesThe UK government first proposed last year that lower-skilled workers wait 10 to 15 years for permanent residency.
Mahmood said the rules would offer a path for care workers “who worked hard and answered our call when we needed them”.

title: Shabana Mahmood poised to massively cut back immigration crackdown in wake of demands from Labour's Left-wing
summary:
Plans to toughen immigration rules are expected to be massively watered down on Monday after a highly damaging battle within the Labour Party.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's proposals to make low-skilled foreign migrants wait far longer for 'settled' status in Britain have been rewritten after strident opposition from her party's Left-wing.
Low-skilled foreign workers and anyone relying on welfare during that time would wait even longer.
Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: 'It's clear Shabana Mahmood has been forced to surrender to Angela Rayner and the open-borders Labour Left.
'After talking tough all year, Mahmood now appears to have capitulated control of immigration policy to Angela Rayner - and Mahmood's position is looking increasingly untenable.'

title: DOJ appeals to Supreme Court to set aside 20,000 California ballots from suspected noncitizens. Here's what to know.
summary:
The Trump administration on Monday appealed to the Supreme Court to order California election officials to set aside mail-in ballots from people it believes are noncitizens.
Election officials say the list is unreliable and likely includes many citizens' names.
In its appeal to the Supreme Court, the Trump administration asked for a "limited injunction" to set aside the ballots while the case plays out.
What does this mean for California voters?
No court has ordered California to set aside any ballots, and counties are still processing the ballots voters return.
